old: Its name once described an action performed by hooves clearing a path through drifts.
The word behind it literally means 'it shovels snow.'
A related Mi'kmaq word, 'qalipi', means 'to shovel snow.'
clues: This hoofed mammal of the far north has a name tracing back to an ancient Algonquian root that literally meant 'it shovels snow'.
A wild deer of North America's tundra, it is the same species as the reindeer but roams untamed in vast migrating herds, and both sexes grow antlers.
It appears on Canada's quarter, and in the Mi'kmaq language of eastern Canada its name is qalipu.
reviewNote: Clue 3 repeated clue 1's 'shovels snow' fact; trimmed to the Mi'kmaq name.
